note: Held-out CrowS-Pairs test split (n=905), Gemma-2-2B + Gemma Scope SAE (JumpReLU, layer 24/26, width 16k, avg_l0_38). All four methods verified deterministic/reproducible across reruns.
direct_activation_note: alpha=1.0, dev-tested (not assumed) via eval/direct_only_sweep.py; sanity-checked to confirm the steering hook fires (nonzero hidden-state perturbation). Dev set showed a tiny +0.17pp gain over baseline at alpha=1.0 (noise, SE~1.9pp on n=603) that did NOT replicate on held-out test -- CrowS came back exactly equal to baseline, confirming direct steering has no real effect on Gemma, consistent with Phi-3.
conclusion: Encoder-SAE steering beats decoder ablation and direct-activation steering on genuinely held-out data, using an independently-trained SAE (Gemma Scope, JumpReLU) on a second model family. Direct-activation steering's alpha was empirically dev-tested (not assumed) and confirmed to have no real effect, replicating Phi-3's finding via a genuine sweep rather than an extrapolated assumption.
